Healthcare / Ophthalmology

GEO for ophthalmology clinics and eye-care centres

Patients ask AI assistants about eye examinations, cataract surgery and retinal services for different reasons. I investigate which clinics are recommended for each need and whether their procedures, clinical staff, licensed locations and appointment information are supported by evidence.

  • Unbranded prompt groups for distinct eye-care services
  • Checks for diagnosis-related services, surgery and provider locations
  • Baseline BMR separated from subsequent recommendation changes

Personally led by Alexey Yakovlev, GEO/AEO consultant

Selection barriers

Why a single generic eye-treatment page is not enough

A person seeking glaucoma monitoring and someone considering refractive surgery need distinct medical information and different service comparisons.

01

Examinations are confused with surgery

Retinal diagnostics, cataract surgery, laser vision correction and routine consultations have different indications, settings and care stages. A procedure mentioned on a website may not be available at every location.

02

Headline fees omit clinical stages

A consultation price may exclude preoperative tests, the procedure and follow-up. Without a defined scope it is misleading to present it as the total treatment fee.

03

Clinician and location facts are detached

A clinician biography and an organisation's licence do not by themselves establish operating facilities, equipment or appointment availability at a particular address.

Verifiable facts

Evidence required for ophthalmology provider claims

I check medical service scope, clinician details and the availability of individual procedures. Russian Health Ministry Order 633n governs adult ophthalmology care from February 2026; it does not endorse a clinic. Medical consent and clinical decisions remain separate from marketing work.

  • Authorised activities and location, relevant clinicians and reliable contact details
  • Available examinations and procedures, preparation, service boundaries and actual staged fees
  • Permissioned evidence, up-to-date physician profiles, truthful scheduling and patient confidentiality

This is an industry GEO approach, not a claim of completed GAEO ophthalmology work or patient outcomes.

Scope of work

How I would structure ophthalmology GEO

The baseline separates examinations, routine treatment and surgery, then compares the sources behind AI recommendations.

  1. 01

    Baseline by eye-care intent

    Record unbranded prompts for examinations, cataract procedures, refractive surgery and follow-up in relevant cities.

  2. 02

    Verify clinical information

    Review licensed work, service locations, clinician profiles, actual procedures, fees and approved data.

  3. 03

    Develop reference pages

    Specify content for departments, real staff, locations, clinical pathways and accurate patient-facing FAQ.

  4. 04

    Repeat the same prompts

    Compare BMR, citations and errors, especially wrong procedures or locations.

FAQ

Questions about the service

Can diagnostic services and eye surgery share one GEO programme?+

Yes, but the pages, intent groups and evidence need to distinguish examinations and surgical procedures. Each service has its own clinical and location constraints.

Does an ophthalmology licence prove every service is offered?+

No. Check the authorised activities at each address and the organisation's verified service list; the existence of a licence is not proof of availability or outcomes.

Can a clinic advertise a successful-surgery rate?+

Only with transparent definitions, cohort, period, method and permission to use the figures. A guaranteed individual vision result must not be inferred.

Will AI decide which treatment a patient needs?+

No. GEO concerns accurate provider descriptions and comparison. Diagnosis and treatment selection belong to qualified clinicians.

What does GAEO charge an ophthalmology clinic?+

The published GAEO tariffs apply. The audit depends on treatment areas, sites, markets and the initial prompt matrix.
